title: Proving all cases and unique solutions
transcript: A proof needs reasons that cover every allowed case. To prove a unique answer, show that it works and that every different answer fails. A bound or an increasing pattern can eliminate an entire range in one step.

AMC practice may ask for the only integer satisfying a clue. Use the constraint to get a narrow range before testing candidates. Mawa application practice rewards clear reasons. A proof can use inequalities, a complete list, or a pattern you justify for all values.
List the multiples of six from twenty-three through thirty-five, counting both endpoints. Explain how you know the list is complete. Find the first eligible multiple and step forward by the divisor.

The first eligible value is twenty-four. The preceding multiple is eighteen, below the lower limit. The full list is twenty-four and thirty. The next multiple is thirty-six, which is already above the upper limit.
Two positive whole numbers add to nineteen. Neither can exceed thirteen. List all pairs, counting a swapped pair only once. Call the smaller number x and use this to bound x from both sides.

The larger number is nineteen minus x, so x is at least six. Since x is the smaller, it is at most nine. Each integer in that range gives exactly one partner. There are four pairs. All of them meet the cap.

An integer-sided rectangle has area two hundred and nine square units. Its longer side is eight units greater than its shorter side. Find its two side lengths and prove that no second pair of positive integer lengths works.

Let x be the shorter side. The area is x times x plus eight, with both terms positive. Try ten for x and check the area. The next integer, eleven, gives eleven times nineteen, exactly two hundred and nine. That proves this pair exists.

Every increase in x increases both positive factors. The area increases strictly. Any x below eleven gives too little area and any x above gives too much. The dimensions are therefore uniquely eleven and nineteen units. They check both the area and the side difference.

One candidate that works proves existence only. Give a bound, exhaustive list or increasing rule to exclude every other candidate. When working with a closed interval, its boundary values are eligible. Test whether the inequality is strict before dropping an endpoint.

State what you need to prove: all answers, at least one answer, or exactly one answer. List the restrictions that define a legal candidate. Use a complete range or a justified relationship. Verify the survivor or survivors in the original problem before writing your answer.
